name: (2015 DM215)
assessment: As the largest and closest visitor today, this 86-meter rock is cruising past at a significant 51,137 km/h. While its size is notable, it remains over 16 million kilometers away, posing absolutely no threat to our global safety.

name: (2017 QB35)
assessment: This compact 8-meter object is essentially a cosmic pebble traveling at a modest speed relative to its peers. Its passage at 27 million kilometers is a non-event for planetary defense, as it would likely disintegrate if it ever encountered an atmosphere.

name: (2013 QF11)
assessment: Blistering through the void at over 64,000 km/h, this 71-meter asteroid is today's fastest-moving tracked object. Fortunately, it maintains a massive cushion of 34 million kilometers, keeping this high-speed traveler firmly in the 'safe' category.
